questions.title: Locked Counter Snippet
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print? (Both threads are joined before printing.)
questions.codesnippet:
import threading

count = 0
lock = threading.Lock()

def work():
    global count
    for _ in range(3):
        with lock:
            count += 1

t1 = threading.Thread(target=work)
t2 = threading.Thread(target=work)
t1.start()
t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()
print(count)

questions.title: run() Versus start()
questions.description: What does this snippet print, and what does it reveal?
questions.Option1: ran then done — job() executes in the main thread, no new thread is created
questions.Option2: ran then done — job() executes in a brand new thread
questions.codesnippet:
import threading

def job():
    print("ran")

t = threading.Thread(target=job)
t.run()
print("done")

questions.title: Slot Filling Threads
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print? (Both threads are joined before the print.)
questions.codesnippet:
import threading

results = [0, 0]

def fill(i, v):
    results[i] = v * v

t1 = threading.Thread(target=fill, args=(0, 4))
t2 = threading.Thread(target=fill, args=(1, 6))
t1.start()
t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()
print(results[0] + results[1])

questions.title: Await Chain Output
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print?
questions.codesnippet:
import asyncio

async def step(x):
    return x + 5

async def main():
    a = await step(10)
    b = await step(a)
    print(a + b)

asyncio.run(main())

questions.title: Lock Reacquire Deadlock
questions.description: What happens when this snippet runs? (Think carefully about whether a plain Lock can be acquired twice by the same thread.)
questions.Option2: It hangs forever — a plain Lock is not reentrant, so the second acquire blocks on a lock its own thread already holds
questions.Option3: It prints inner, then raises RuntimeError
questions.Option4: The with statement silently allows nested acquisition, so both lines print
questions.codesnippet:
import threading

lock = threading.Lock()

def risky():
    with lock:
        with lock:
            print("inner")

risky()
print("after")

questions.title: gather Order and Sum
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print?
questions.codesnippet:
import asyncio

async def val(x):
    return x * 2

async def main():
    r = await asyncio.gather(val(1), val(5), val(10))
    print(sum(r), r[0])

asyncio.run(main())

questions.title: Daemon Thread Lifetime
questions.description: What does this snippet do? (spin loops forever, but the thread is a daemon.)
questions.Option1: It prints bye and the process exits, cutting off the still-running daemon loop
questions.Option3: It prints bye, then the daemon raises SystemExit in the main thread
questions.Option4: start() refuses to launch a daemon thread that loops forever
questions.codesnippet:
import threading

def spin():
    while True:
        pass

t = threading.Thread(target=spin, daemon=True)
t.start()
print("bye")

questions.title: Why the GIL Is Not Enough
questions.description: Why can the statement count += 1 executed by several threads still misbehave in CPython even though the GIL allows only one thread to run bytecodes at a time?
questions.Option1: The statement compiles to several bytecodes (read, add, write) and a thread switch can happen between them
questions.Option2: The GIL blocks all shared memory access, causing lost updates
questions.Option3: count += 1 is fully atomic, so it can never misbehave
questions.Option4: The GIL only protects file objects, not integers
